topic: The Teacher and the Community, School Culture and Organizational Leadership
subtopic: RA 9155, School-Based Management, Leadership Models, & School Culture

items.term: Republic Act No. 9155 (Governance of Basic Education Act of 2001)
items.definition: The landmark Philippine law that decentralized educational management, instituting the principle of shared governance and empowering school heads with authority, accountability, and responsibility.
items.rationalization: Renamed the Department of Education, Culture and Sports (DECS) to the Department of Education (DepEd), transferring cultural agencies to NCCA and sports to the PSC.

mnemonic.title: RA 9155 Decentralization
mnemonic.phrase: 9155 = School-Based Governance and Empowerment

items.tosCompetency: Analyze RA 9155 and school decentralization governance

items.definition: The administrative principle where every unit in the educational hierarchy (central, regional, division, school) has a particular role, task, and responsibility, but decisions are made collaboratively.
items.rationalization: Recognizes the school as the heart of the formal education system; higher administrative offices exist primarily to support, mentor, and resource school-level learning.

mnemonic.title: Shared Governance
mnemonic.phrase: School at the Center, Supported by All Levels

items.tosCompetency: Analyze RA 9155 and school decentralization governance

items.definition: A decentralized strategy that transfers the decision-making authority over budget, personnel, and curriculum from central and division offices directly to the individual school community.
items.rationalization: Empowers the school principal, teachers, parents, students, and community members to identify local needs and design localized solutions via the School Improvement Plan (SIP).

mnemonic.title: SBM Essence
mnemonic.phrase: Decisions Made by Those Closest to the Classroom

items.tosCompetency: Evaluate School-Based Management (SBM) levels and implementation

items.definition: The three progressive maturity levels of School-Based Management: Level I (Developing - basic structures initiated); Level II (Maturing - collaborative continuous improvement); Level III (Advanced - self-sustaining accredited excellence).
items.rationalization: Assessed across 4 principles: Leadership & Governance, Curriculum & Learning, Accountability & Continuous Improvement, and Management of Resources.

mnemonic.title: 3 SBM Levels
mnemonic.phrase: Level 1 Developing, Level 2 Maturing, Level 3 Advanced

items.tosCompetency: Evaluate School-Based Management (SBM) levels and implementation

items.term: Edgar Schein's Three Levels of Organizational Culture
items.definition: The organizational framework dividing school culture into three layers: 1. Artifacts (visible symbols, ceremonies, dress code); 2. Espoused Values (stated mission, vision, slogans); 3. Basic Underlying Assumptions (deep unconscious beliefs and worldviews).
items.rationalization: True cultural reform requires changing basic underlying assumptions; simply painting new school mottos (espoused values) leaves deep school culture unchanged.

mnemonic.title: Schein's 3 Layers
mnemonic.phrase: Artifacts (Surface), Espoused Values (Motto), Assumptions (Core)

items.tosCompetency: Analyze organizational school culture and climate frameworks

items.definition: School Culture refers to the deep, historical values, traditions, unwritten rules, and assumptions developed over decades; School Climate refers to the current psychological feeling, morale, safety, and immediate atmosphere of the school ('the weather').
items.rationalization: School climate can change quickly with a new charismatic principal; school culture is deeply entrenched and takes years of persistent collaborative effort to shift.

mnemonic.title: Culture vs Climate
mnemonic.phrase: Culture is the Climate Over Decades; Climate is the Current Weather

items.tosCompetency: Analyze organizational school culture and climate frameworks

items.definition: A leadership theory where leaders inspire, motivate, and intellectually stimulate followers to transcend self-interest and work collaboratively toward a visionary, transcendent organizational goal.
items.rationalization: Characterized by the 4 Is: Idealized Influence (role modeling), Inspirational Motivation (vision), Intellectual Stimulation (challenging assumptions), and Individualized Consideration (coaching).

mnemonic.title: Transformational 4 Is
mnemonic.phrase: Influence, Inspiration, Intellectual stimulation, Individualized coaching

items.tosCompetency: Compare educational leadership styles and administrative models

items.definition: A leadership philosophy asserting that the primary duty of an educational leader is to serve others (teachers, students, parents) first, prioritizing their growth and well-being over personal power.
items.rationalization: Characteristics include active listening, empathy, healing, self-awareness, persuasion rather than coercion, stewardship, and building authentic community.

mnemonic.title: Servant Leader
mnemonic.phrase: Leader as Servant First, Boss Second

items.tosCompetency: Compare educational leadership styles and administrative models

items.definition: A school leadership approach focused primarily on the core business of schooling: improving curriculum delivery, supervising classroom instruction, mentoring teachers, and analyzing student achievement data.
items.rationalization: The school head spends significant time in classrooms observing instruction and providing clinical supervision rather than remaining trapped behind an office desk doing administrative paperwork.

mnemonic.title: Instructional Leader
mnemonic.phrase: Focused on Curriculum, Teaching Quality, and Student Learning

items.tosCompetency: Compare educational leadership styles and administrative models

items.definition: A leadership model that views leadership not as the monopoly of a single heroic principal, but as a collective activity distributed across teachers, department chairs, and staff throughout the school.
items.rationalization: Fosters teacher leadership and professional agency; recognizes that teachers possess specialized pedagogical expertise that enriches school decision-making.

mnemonic.title: Distributed Leadership
mnemonic.phrase: Leadership is Stretched Over Many People

items.tosCompetency: Compare educational leadership styles and administrative models

items.definition: A leadership framework stating that effective leadership depends on matching the leader's style (Telling, Selling, Participating, Delegating) to the maturity and competence level of the followers.
items.rationalization: Directing/Telling is used for new, inexperienced teachers; Delegating is used for highly competent, confident master teachers.

mnemonic.title: Situational 4 Styles
mnemonic.phrase: T-S-P-D: Telling, Selling, Participating, Delegating

items.tosCompetency: Compare educational leadership styles and administrative models

items.definition: DepEd's nationwide community-based initiative mobilizing teachers, parents, students, local government units, alumni, and private partners to repair, clean, and prepare public schools before classes open.
items.rationalization: The modern embodiment of the traditional Filipino 'Bayanihan' spirit; demonstrates that public education is a collective community responsibility, not the government's burden alone.

mnemonic.title: Brigada Eskwela
mnemonic.phrase: Bayanihan in Action: Community Cleans the School

items.tosCompetency: Design school-community partnership programs (Brigada Eskwela, Adopt-a-School)

items.definition: The Philippine law encouraging private sector entities, business corporations, and alumni to assist public schools in remote and disadvantaged areas by offering a 150% tax incentive deduction.
items.rationalization: Enables private companies to donate classrooms, science laboratories, computer packages, and teacher trainings in exchange for tax credits.

mnemonic.title: RA 8525 Adopt-a-School
mnemonic.phrase: 8525 = 150% Tax Deduction for Private School Donors

items.tosCompetency: Design school-community partnership programs (Brigada Eskwela, Adopt-a-School)

items.term: Parent-Teacher Association (PTA / DepEd Order No. 54 s. 2009)
items.definition: The recognized school-level organization of parents, guardians, and teachers formed to foster harmonious relations, finance school improvements, and safeguard student welfare.
items.rationalization: Strict rules: Membership contributions must be voluntary and approved by majority vote; collection of fees is strictly prohibited during enrollment or exam periods.

mnemonic.title: PTA Guidelines
mnemonic.phrase: Voluntary Support, No Coercive Fees During Enrollment

items.tosCompetency: Apply DepEd policies on PTAs and School Governing Councils

items.definition: The apex policy-making and advisory body at the school level composed of the principal, teachers, parents, students, LGU officials, and community leaders ensuring transparent accountability.
items.rationalization: Provides broad community oversight, assists in formulating the School Improvement Plan (SIP), and ensures school programs reflect local cultural and economic needs.

mnemonic.title: SGC Policy Body
mnemonic.phrase: Community Stakeholder Board for School Governance

items.tosCompetency: Apply DepEd policies on PTAs and School Governing Councils

items.definition: A roadmap that lays out the school's three-year strategic goals, priorities, interventions, and financial plans to improve student learning outcomes and school environment.
items.rationalization: Developed participatory-style by the School-Community Planning Team (SPT) using data from the School Report Card (SRC) and Child-Friendly School System (CFSS).

mnemonic.title: SIP Roadmap
mnemonic.phrase: Three-Year Strategic Roadmap for School Excellence

items.tosCompetency: Analyze the School Improvement Plan (SIP) and Continuous Improvement (CI)

items.definition: The yearly operational blueprint derived directly from the three-year School Improvement Plan (SIP), outlining specific annual projects, activities, budget allocations, and performance indicators.
items.rationalization: Breaks down long-term 3-year objectives into manageable, measurable 12-month action steps funded by the school's Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE).

mnemonic.title: AIP Operational
mnemonic.phrase: One-Year Action Plan Derived from the SIP

items.tosCompetency: Analyze the School Improvement Plan (SIP) and Continuous Improvement (CI)

items.term: Learning Action Cell (LAC / DepEd Order No. 35 s. 2016)
items.definition: A school-based professional learning community (PLC) where teachers meet regularly in small collaborative groups to engage in reflective dialogue, solve curriculum challenges, and improve teaching practice.
items.rationalization: The primary school-based continuing professional development strategy in DepEd, utilizing peer mentoring, lesson study, and action research to elevate student learning.

mnemonic.title: LAC Sessions
mnemonic.phrase: DO 35 s. 2016: Teachers Learning Together Every Month

items.tosCompetency: Implement Learning Action Cell (LAC) sessions and Professional Learning Communities

items.definition: A conflict resolution model based on two dimensions (Assertiveness and Cooperativeness) identifying five conflict styles: Competing, Collaborating, Compromising, Avoiding, and Accommodating.
items.rationalization: Collaborating is the ideal win-win style (high assertiveness, high cooperativeness); Compromising finds a middle ground; Avoiding is appropriate when tensions are dangerously high and cooling down is needed.

mnemonic.title: 5 Conflict Styles
mnemonic.phrase: Compete (Win-Lose), Collaborate (Win-Win), Compromise (Split), Avoid, Accommodate

items.tosCompetency: Apply conflict resolution strategies and collaborative decision-making

items.definition: The conflict management approach where both parties work together assertively and cooperatively to find a creative, integrative solution that fully satisfies the concerns of both sides.
items.rationalization: Best used when long-term relationships and mutual buy-in are vital (e.g., resolving curriculum disagreements between teachers and parents).

mnemonic.title: Collaborating Style
mnemonic.phrase: Win-Win: Both Sides Truly Satisfied

items.tosCompetency: Apply conflict resolution strategies and collaborative decision-making

items.definition: The conflict management approach where both parties give up something to find an expedient, mutually acceptable middle ground that partially satisfies both.
items.rationalization: Appropriate when time is scarce and a temporary, practical truce is needed, though neither party achieves complete satisfaction.

mnemonic.title: Compromising Style
mnemonic.phrase: Split the Difference: Both Give a Little

items.tosCompetency: Apply conflict resolution strategies and collaborative decision-making

items.term: Toxic School Culture vs Collegial School Culture
items.definition: A toxic school culture is plagued by gossip, cynicism, resistance to change, isolation, and fragmentation; A collegial culture fosters professional collaboration, high expectations, transparent trust, and celebration of teacher success.
items.rationalization: Educational leaders dismantle toxic cultures by establishing psychological safety, modeling ethical integrity, and recognizing positive peer innovations.

mnemonic.title: School Culture Contrast
mnemonic.phrase: Toxic Divides and Blames; Collegial Unites and Builds

items.tosCompetency: Analyze organizational school culture and climate frameworks

items.definition: The sociological principle recognizing that the school and the community are symbiotic partners: the community provides cultural heritage, resources, and students, while the school supplies educated citizens and civic leadership.
items.rationalization: Schools that isolate themselves behind high walls fail; community-engaged schools utilize local farms, workshops, and elders as rich living textbooks.

mnemonic.title: Symbiotic Partnership
mnemonic.phrase: It Takes a Whole Village to Educate a Child

items.tosCompetency: Design school-community partnership programs (Brigada Eskwela, Adopt-a-School)

items.definition: The public school operational budget allocated by the national government to fund daily utilities, learning materials, office supplies, building maintenance, and minor school repairs.
items.rationalization: Liquidation of MOOE must be displayed publicly on the school's Transparency Board to uphold good governance and accountability under RA 9155.

mnemonic.title: School MOOE
mnemonic.phrase: MOOE = Public Operational Budget on Transparency Board

items.tosCompetency: Analyze RA 9155 and school decentralization governance

items.definition: A prominent bulletin board located at the school entrance displaying the school's budget allocations, MOOE disbursements, PTA financial reports, and academic performance indicators.
items.rationalization: Enforces anti-corruption standards and strengthens community trust by keeping fiscal management open to public scrutiny.

mnemonic.title: Transparency Board
mnemonic.phrase: Public Financial Receipts Build Community Trust

items.tosCompetency: Analyze RA 9155 and school decentralization governance

items.definition: A public accountability and communication tool produced annually by the school head to inform parents, community partners, and stakeholders of the school's academic achievements, dropout rates, and resource gaps.
items.rationalization: Presents vital data (National Achievement Test scores, retention rates, enrollment trends) in simple visual infographics to guide community-driven interventions.

mnemonic.title: School Report Card
mnemonic.phrase: The School's Annual Performance Showcase

items.tosCompetency: Evaluate School-Based Management (SBM) levels and implementation

items.definition: A structured methodology utilizing the DMAIC (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control) problem-solving approach to continually eliminate waste and improve school delivery processes.
items.rationalization: Focuses on school-level pain points (e.g., reducing non-readers in Grade 3, speeding up enrollment queuing, reducing tardiness) through evidence-based cycles.

mnemonic.title: CI Program DMAIC
mnemonic.phrase: Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control

items.tosCompetency: Analyze the School Improvement Plan (SIP) and Continuous Improvement (CI)

items.definition: A managerial leadership approach based on an exchange of rewards or sanctions for employee compliance, focusing on maintaining existing routines, rules, and contractual obligations.
items.rationalization: Uses Contingent Reward (bonus for meeting target) and Management by Exception (intervening only when things go wrong); good for administrative order, but fails to inspire vision.

mnemonic.title: Transactional Model
mnemonic.phrase: Rewards for Compliance, Penalties for Errors

items.tosCompetency: Compare educational leadership styles and administrative models

items.definition: A passive, hands-off leadership style where the school head abdicates decision-making authority, leaving staff without clear guidance, feedback, or supervision.
items.rationalization: Often results in organizational drift, confusion, low teacher accountability, and school climate deterioration.

mnemonic.title: Laissez-Faire Style
mnemonic.phrase: Hands-Off, Total Abdication of Direction

items.tosCompetency: Compare educational leadership styles and administrative models

items.definition: A directive leadership style where the school head makes all decisions unilaterally without consulting teachers or staff, demanding unquestioning obedience.
items.rationalization: Effective during immediate crisis management, but crushes teacher morale, squashes innovation, and breeds resentful compliance.

mnemonic.title: Autocratic Leader
mnemonic.phrase: One-Way Top-Down Command

items.tosCompetency: Compare educational leadership styles and administrative models

items.definition: A leadership style where the school head encourages staff, parents, and teachers to participate actively in decision-making and policy formation.
items.rationalization: Builds high organizational commitment and team consensus, though decision-making can be slower due to collaborative consultation.

mnemonic.title: Democratic Leader
mnemonic.phrase: Shared Voices, Consensus Decision-Making

items.tosCompetency: Compare educational leadership styles and administrative models

items.definition: A shared belief that the school team is safe for interpersonal risk-taking, where teachers feel secure speaking up, asking for help, proposing new ideas, and admitting mistakes without fear of ridicule or retaliation.
items.rationalization: Harvard research proves psychological safety is the single most critical factor distinguishing high-performing teacher teams from mediocre ones.

mnemonic.title: Psychological Safety
mnemonic.phrase: Safe to Admit Mistakes and Propose Ideas

items.tosCompetency: Analyze organizational school culture and climate frameworks

items.definition: DepEd's comprehensive institutionalized transition program providing structured orientation, mentorship, and pedagogical support to newly hired teachers during their first three years.
items.rationalization: Reduces early teacher attrition and burn-out, assisting Beginning Teachers to master DepEd systems and PPST proficiencies.

mnemonic.title: TIP Program
mnemonic.phrase: Three-Year Mentorship for New Teachers

items.tosCompetency: Implement Learning Action Cell (LAC) sessions and Professional Learning Communities

items.term: Clinical Supervision in Education (Goldhammer and Cogan)
items.definition: A collegial, non-evaluative supervisory process focused on improving classroom instruction through a 5-step cycle: Pre-observation conference, Observation, Analysis, Post-observation conference, and Post-conference analysis.
items.rationalization: Replaces intimidating inspection visits; the supervisor and teacher collaborate as professional partners to analyze objective teaching evidence.

mnemonic.title: Clinical Supervision
mnemonic.phrase: Pre-Conference, Observation, Post-Conference Dialogue

items.tosCompetency: Apply instructional supervision models and clinical observation

items.definition: The formal administrative procedure established to resolve employee complaints and labor dissatisfaction at the lowest possible level before escalating to legal tribunals.
items.rationalization: Ensures harmonious labor relations; grievances begin with the immediate supervisor and move through school, division, and regional grievance committees.

mnemonic.title: Grievance Procedure
mnemonic.phrase: Resolve Disagreements at the Lowest Level First

items.tosCompetency: Apply conflict resolution strategies and collaborative decision-making

items.definition: The systematic process of identifying, consulting, and involving internal stakeholders (teachers, students) and external stakeholders (alumni, LGU, NGOs, business donors) in school policy development.
items.rationalization: Broad stakeholder buy-in ensures that educational programs survive changes in local political administrations and remain community-rooted.

mnemonic.title: Stakeholder Buy-In
mnemonic.phrase: Involve the Whole Community for Enduring Success

items.tosCompetency: Design school-community partnership programs (Brigada Eskwela, Adopt-a-School)

items.term: Local School Board (LSB / Local Government Code RA 7160)
items.definition: The provincial, city, or municipal body co-chaired by the Local Chief Executive (Governor/Mayor) and the Division Superintendent/District Supervisor, managing the Special Education Fund (SEF).
items.rationalization: Determines how the SEF tax collections are spent on constructing local school buildings, purchasing textbooks, and hiring supplementary volunteer teachers.

mnemonic.title: Local School Board
mnemonic.phrase: Mayor and Superintendent Direct the SEF Fund

items.tosCompetency: Analyze RA 9155 and school decentralization governance

items.definition: A dedicated local tax fund generated from an additional 1% tax on real property collected by local government units, exclusively designated for public education financing.
items.rationalization: Funds the construction of classrooms, sports facilities, teacher training allowances, and emergency educational equipment under the direction of the Local School Board.

mnemonic.title: SEF Real Property Tax
mnemonic.phrase: 1% Real Estate Tax for Local Schools

items.tosCompetency: Analyze RA 9155 and school decentralization governance

items.definition: The capacity of a school head to perceive, regulate, and express emotions accurately and empathetically when managing teacher faculty and stressful community crises.
items.rationalization: Leaders with high EQ build trusting organizational climates, de-escalate faculty conflicts gracefully, and shield staff from burn-out.

mnemonic.title: EQ Leadership
mnemonic.phrase: Empathy and Self-Regulation Before Authority

items.tosCompetency: Compare educational leadership styles and administrative models

items.term: Change Management: Kurt Lewin's Three-Step Model
items.definition: A foundational change framework for school organizational transitions: 1. Unfreezing (breaking comfortable status quo habits); 2. Changing/Transition (adopting new behaviors/curricula); 3. Refreezing (institutionalizing new practices into school culture).
items.rationalization: Educational leaders who skip 'unfreezing' face fierce faculty resistance because teachers do not understand why change is necessary.

mnemonic.title: Lewin's 3 Steps
mnemonic.phrase: Unfreeze, Change, Refreeze

items.tosCompetency: Analyze organizational school culture and climate frameworks

items.definition: A critical race framework highlighting the rich array of knowledge, skills, abilities, and contacts possessed by marginalized and indigenous communities: Aspirational, Linguistic, Familial, Social, Navigational, and Resistant capital.
items.rationalization: Challenges deficit thinking; teachers view poor or indigenous students as entering school rich with ancestral resilience, bilingual agility, and community wisdom.

mnemonic.title: Yosso's Cultural Wealth
mnemonic.phrase: Deficit Thinking Eradicated: Culture is Capital

items.tosCompetency: Design school-community partnership programs (Brigada Eskwela, Adopt-a-School)

items.definition: A joint DepEd and UNICEF initiative setting standards for schools to be inclusive, gender-sensitive, child-centered, healthy, protective of children, and actively engaging of families.
items.rationalization: Focuses on the rights and holistic well-being of the whole child, evaluating sanitation, nutrition, clean water, and emotional safety alongside exam scores.

mnemonic.title: Child-Friendly School
mnemonic.phrase: Safe, Healthy, Inclusive, Child-Centered

items.tosCompetency: Apply child protection policies and school child rights protocols

items.term: Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (DRRM in Schools / RA 10121)
items.definition: The institutional protocol in Philippine schools establishing safety drills, disaster evacuation maps, student emergency kits, and School DRRM Teams to prepare for earthquakes, typhoons, and fires.
items.rationalization: The Philippines' location in the typhoon belt and Pacific Ring of Fire requires mandatory quarterly nationwide earthquake drills in every public school.

mnemonic.title: School DRRM
mnemonic.phrase: Duck, Cover, Hold: Disaster Preparedness for All

items.tosCompetency: Implement school safety, emergency, and DRRM protocols

items.definition: Parent involvement is passive participation where parents simply attend meetings when summoned or donate money; Parent engagement is active, collaborative partnership where parents co-design student learning goals with teachers.
items.rationalization: Parent engagement creates shared ownership of educational success, resulting in significantly higher student attendance and achievement.

mnemonic.title: Engagement vs Involvement
mnemonic.phrase: Involvement is Doing To; Engagement is Doing With

items.tosCompetency: Design school-community partnership programs (Brigada Eskwela, Adopt-a-School)

items.definition: A structured, ongoing professional relationship where experienced master teachers coach, advise, and nurture beginning teachers in pedagogy, classroom management, and ethics.
items.rationalization: Fosters collegiality and instructional consistency across grade levels, turning isolated teaching silos into vibrant learning ecosystems.

mnemonic.title: Teacher Mentorship
mnemonic.phrase: Master Teachers Nurturing Novices

items.tosCompetency: Implement Learning Action Cell (LAC) sessions and Professional Learning Communities

items.definition: The professional obligation of educational leaders and teachers to administer public school funds, physical facilities, and donations with absolute honesty, transparency, and frugality.
items.rationalization: Upholds the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials (RA 6713); strictly bans misappropriation of school property for personal gain.

mnemonic.title: Ethical Stewardship
mnemonic.phrase: Public Funds Dedicated Exclusively to Student Learning

items.tosCompetency: Apply the Code of Ethics for Professional Teachers to ethical dilemmas

items.definition: A school's Vision describes its inspiring future aspiration (what it dreams to achieve), while its Mission defines its core daily purpose, primary beneficiaries, and operational commitments.
items.rationalization: Aligns all teachers and staff toward common organizational goals, guiding instructional priorities and school improvement plans.

mnemonic.title: Vision vs Mission
mnemonic.phrase: Vision is the Future Dream; Mission is the Daily Work
items: Vision: Where we want to be
Mission: What we do every single day

items.tosCompetency: Analyze organizational school culture and climate frameworks

items.definition: A collaborative professional development strategy where two colleagues observe each other's classes, discuss pedagogical strategies, and provide non-judgmental reflective feedback.
items.rationalization: Fosters horizontal peer accountability without administrative grading pressure, encouraging teachers to experiment with innovative teaching techniques.

mnemonic.title: Peer Coaching
mnemonic.phrase: Teachers Observing Teachers for Mutual Growth

items.tosCompetency: Implement Learning Action Cell (LAC) sessions and Professional Learning Communities

items.definition: An assessment process where schools identify the collective resources, talents, businesses, cultural elders, and institutions available within the local community that can enrich student learning.
items.rationalization: Replaces deficit perspectives with an appreciative inquiry approach; turns barangay carpenters, clinics, and artists into experiential classroom partners.

mnemonic.title: Asset Mapping
mnemonic.phrase: Cataloging Community Strengths for Education

items.tosCompetency: Design school-community partnership programs (Brigada Eskwela, Adopt-a-School)

items.definition: The ethical and administrative principle that professional educators share responsibility for student academic growth, continuously reflecting on assessment data to refine their instructional practice.
items.rationalization: Rejects blaming student socioeconomic background for low scores; effective teachers proactively differentiate instruction to ensure every learner achieves mastery.

mnemonic.title: Teacher Accountability
mnemonic.phrase: Taking Ownership of Every Child's Academic Growth

items.tosCompetency: Analyze RA 9155 and school decentralization governance
